Your daily reminder that free market & capitalism are two exact opposites : Dean W. Ball (@deanwball) Some observations on Kimi: 1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run. 2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China. 3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "the art of not being governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex. 4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure." This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business. 5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this. 6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/deanwball/status/2078133895766114412#m

250,000 books. That is how many my Ukrainian publisher, Knygolove knigolove.ua/ lost on 19 July after three Russian Iskander missiles struck the warehouse outside Kyiv. Among them were my books, too. This is war, and war inevitably brings human and material losses. But when books burn, it is not just paper that burns. Culture, memory, and identity burn with them. So does a nation’s right to grow and shape its own future. That is why burning books has always meant far more than destroying merchandise. I have waived my royalties for the next year to help support my publisher. I encourage you to buy Ukrainian books—as a gesture of solidarity with Ukrainians fighting, among other things, for the right to read books in their own language. Books survive as long as there are people to print them and people to read them.

Dr. Joram Aniya, Member, NITI Aayog, visited Gyekar Sinyik (Ganga Lake) in Arunachal Pradesh to assess its potential for sustainable eco-tourism and discuss measures to strengthen climate resilience and disaster preparedness. Senior officials from NITI Aayog, NDMA, the Central Water Commission, and other concerned agencies were also present. The visit included discussions with local officials and communities on the need for scientific studies of the lake's hydrology, geology, and catchment dynamics to better understand changing water levels and inform long-term risk mitigation strategies. The delegation also explored sustainable and technically feasible measures to preserve the lake's ecological integrity while reducing disaster risks. Dr. Joram Aniya emphasised the importance of balancing environmental conservation with scientific planning and community well-being to promote sustainable development in ecologically fragile regions. The visit reaffirmed NITI Aayog's commitment to advancing climate resilience, ecological stewardship, and sustainable tourism in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. #ArunachalPradesh #SustainableTourism @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

मराठी भाषा संवर्धनासाठी राज्य मराठी विकास संस्थेला अधिक सक्षम करण्यावर भर मुख्यमंत्री देवेंद्र फडणवीस यांच्या अध्यक्षतेखाली आज सह्याद्री अतिथीगृह, मुंबई येथे 'राज्य मराठी विकास संस्थे'च्या नियामक मंडळाची बैठक पार पडली. राज्य मराठी विकास संस्थेच्या कामकाजात सातत्य, पारदर्शकता आणि परिणामकारकता यावी, यासाठी वर्षभरातील सर्व वैधानिक बैठकींचे वेळापत्रक पूर्वनियोजन करून निश्चित करावे. तसेच प्रभावी कृती आराखडा तयार करून त्याची अंमलबजावणी करावी, असे निर्देश मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी दिले. राज्य मराठी विकास संस्थेची सर्व वैधानिक अनुपालने पूर्ण झाल्याबद्दल संस्थेचे अभिनंदन करत मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस म्हणाले, संस्थेतील गेल्या काही वर्षांपासूनचा प्रशासकीय व वैधानिक अनुशेष दूर झाल्याने संस्थेची प्रशासकीय रचना अधिक सक्षम व परिणामकारक झाली आहे. आता मराठी भाषेचा प्रचार, प्रसार, संशोधन आणि संवर्धन यासाठी ठोस धोरणे राबविण्यावर भर देणे आवश्यक आहे. संस्थेच्या कर्मचाऱ्यांचे प्रलंबित प्रश्नही सकारात्मक भूमिकेतून सोडविण्यात येतील. या बैठकीत सदस्यांनी मराठी भाषा आणि विविध बोलींच्या संवर्धनासाठी अनेक महत्त्वपूर्ण सूचना मांडल्या. 'पुस्तकांचे गाव' आणि 'पेटी वाचनालय' उपक्रमांचा विस्तार करून आदिवासी व सीमावर्ती भागातील मराठी शाळांपर्यंत दर्जेदार साहित्य पोहोचविणे, झाडीबोली आणि पूर्व विदर्भातील नाट्यपरंपरेच्या जतनासाठी गडचिरोली-वडसा परिसरात नाट्यसंकुल उभारणे, भारुड, गोंधळ, पोवाडा यांसारख्या लोककलांच्या माध्यमातून मराठीचा वारसा जपणे, तसेच बालसाहित्य व बालग्रंथालयांना प्रोत्साहन देण्याबाबत सूचना मांडल्या. या सर्व सूचनांचा सकारात्मकतेने विचार करण्यात येईल, असे मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी सांगितले. मुख्यमंत्री फडणवीस यांनी यावेळी तंजावर येथील मोडी लिपीतील सुमारे 15 लाख ऐतिहासिक कागदपत्रांच्या डिजिटायझेशन प्रकल्पाच्या प्रगतीचा आढावा घेतला. तसेच लंडन येथे महाराष्ट्राचे आराध्यदैवत छत्रपती शिवाजी महाराज यांच्या नावाने उभारण्यात येणाऱ्या जागतिक मराठी केंद्राच्या कामाला गती देण्याबाबतही चर्चा झाली. यावेळी मंत्री उदय सामंत, महाराष्ट्र राज्य साहित्य आणि संस्कृती मंडळाचे अध्यक्ष, ज्येष्ठ साहित्यिक प्रा. सदानंद मोरे, राज्य मराठी विकास संस्थेचे संचालक डॉ. श्यामकांत देवरे आणि वरिष्ठ अधिकारी उपस्थित होते. @Dev_Fadnavis @samant_uday #Maharashtra #DevendraFadnavis #मराठीभाषा

The European Union is Kenya's largest single export destination and a strategic bilateral partner. Our decades-long relations have been boosted by the signing of the European Partnership Agreement (EPA) in July 2024. The EPA provides Kenyan goods, including cut flowers, tea, coffee, and horticulture, duty-free free and quota-free access to the EU market. On its part, the European Union exports to Kenya machinery, chemical and mineral products. Since the signing of EPA, our trade has increased by 20 per cent, bringing annual trade to $3.8 billion (KSh494 billion). Our comprehensive relationship also spans digital innovation, climate resilience and regional security. Bid farewell to European Union Ambassador Henriette Geiger at State House Nairobi. During the time the envoy represented the EU in our country, our ties have significantly strengthened.

Kenya and Belgium share strong bilateral and diplomatic relations anchored on trade and investment, renewable energy and climate action. These ties have been boosted by my recent business roundtable in Brussels in June 2026. On trade, Belgium is the leading destination for Kenyan coffee. Consequently, many businesses in that country have expressed interest in agri-business investment. Bid farewell to Belgium Ambassador Peter Maddens, who has completed his tour of duty in Kenya. Wished him well on his next assignment.

The ASEAN Secretariat participated in the ASEAN-India Scale Hub 2026 held in Bali, Indonesia, from 15–17 July 2026. The programme convened over 334 participants, including 57 growth-stage scale-ups from ASEAN Member States and India, alongside investors, policymakers, technology providers, and ecosystem partners to explore opportunities for regional expansion, investment, and collaboration. Through curated business matchmaking sessions, smart pitches, workshops, and high-level discussions, participants exchanged insights on artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation, startup scaling, enterprise partnerships, and innovation-driven growth, aiming to translate innovative ideas into sustainable commercial opportunities across ASEAN and India. This year's edition also marked an important milestone with the first participation of Timor-Leste and a stronger emphasis on growth-stage and deep-tech enterprises. Unlike previous editions, the programme featured focused discussions on scaling AI-driven businesses, while providing structured opportunities for scale-ups to engage directly with investors, technology providers, and ecosystem leaders across the region. Rome conquered Greece in 146 BC when they burned Corinth to the ground. And then the strangest thing in ancient history happened. The winners spent the next few centuries desperately trying to become the losers. It actually started before the final conquest. When the general Marcellus sacked Syracuse in 211 BC, he shipped boatloads of Greek statues and paintings back to Rome, and the city went crazy for it. Suddenly every rich Roman had to have Greek art in his house. Decades later Cicero built an entire court case around prosecuting a governor named Verres for looting Greek masterpieces, and Romans ate it up. Then came the schools. Wealthy families started buying Greek slaves specifically because they were educated, and handed them the job of raising their children. So the sons of the men who crushed Greece grew up speaking Greek, memorizing Greek poetry, and learning philosophy from Greeks. The elite eventually sent their teenagers abroad to Athens and Rhodes to finish their education, the way people today send kids to study overseas. Cicero did it. Julius Caesar did it. Their gods were Greek gods wearing name tags. Zeus became Jupiter. Hera became Juno. Aphrodite became Venus. Ares became Mars. Same myths, same family drama, mostly just relabeled. Their entertainment was borrowed too. The first big Roman playwrights, Plautus and Terence, basically adapted Greek comedies into Latin. Their doctors were Greek. Their architecture leaned on Greek columns, the Doric and Ionic and Corinthian orders you still see on bank buildings today. And the art obsession left a strange fingerprint on history. Romans loved Greek bronze statues so much that they mass produced marble copies of them. A huge chunk of what people walk past in museums today and call "Greek sculpture" is actually a Roman copy. The Greek originals melted down or vanished long ago. The knockoffs are what survived. Not everyone was thrilled. Cato the Elder spent his whole life warning that Greek culture would rot the Roman character. He sneered at Greek philosophers, distrusted Greek doctors, and wanted them kept out of the city. And then, as an old man, he quietly sat down and learned Greek anyway. Even the loudest hater caved. The trend went all the way to the top. Virgil wrote the Aeneid, Rome's national epic, by openly modeling it on Homer. The emperor Nero competed in Greek games and toured Greece like a superfan. Hadrian was so obsessed he grew a Greek philosopher's beard and poured money into rebuilding Athens. And Marcus Aurelius, master of the entire Roman world, wrote his private journal not in Latin but in Greek, because that was the language of serious thinking. The poet Horace nailed it in a single line: captured Greece took her savage conqueror captive. Rome won every war on the battlefield and then handed its whole soul to the people it had beaten.

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif witnesses the signing of a Protocol on Phyto-Sanitary regulations governing the import of Canola from Canada to Pakistan. Islamabad, 20 July, 2026.
H.E. Ms. Anita Anand, Foreign Minister of Canada calls on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif. Islamabad, 20 July, 2026.

Islamabad : 20 July , 2026. H.E. Ms. Anita Anand, Foreign Minister of Canada, who is on an official visit to Pakistan, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House, earlier today. Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Sen. Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Minister for National Food Security Rana Tanveer Hussain, Advisor to the Prime Minister Dr. Syed Tauqir Shah, and other senior government officials were also present. During the warm and cordial meeting, the Prime Minister welcomed the Canadian Foreign Minister to Pakistan and stated that the two countries enjoyed friendly ties that needed to be further expanded, particularly in the areas of trade, investment, agriculture including agri-foods and vaccine manufacturing, renewable energy, as well as the automobile and auto parts industry. He conveyed his greetings and best wishes for Prime Minister Mark Carney and said that he looked forward to meeting him soon. He fondly recalled the telephone conversation with his Canadian counterpart in April, and thanked Canada for supporting Pakistan’s regional peace efforts. Foreign Minister Anita Anand thanked the Prime Minister for the warm welcome accorded to her and her delegation in Islamabad. She conveyed the good wishes of Prime Minister Carney for the Prime Minister and said that her visit was on the instructions of her Prime Minister to expand Canada’s relations with Pakistan. On the bilateral front, the Canadian Foreign Minister expressed the keen desire of her Government to explore new opportunities for trade and cooperation, especially in the field of agriculture, mining, energy as well as in the auto and auto parts industry. In this regard, she said the Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPPA) would be instrumental in enhancing Canadian investors’ confidence to invest in Pakistan. Both sides agreed that the Pakistani Canadian community was acting as a vital bridge between the two nations. The two sides also agreed to exchange delegations in the fields of trade and minerals cooperation, to explore mutually beneficial opportunities, with a view to further enhance bilateral trade and investment prospects. After the meeting, the Prime Minister witnessed the signing of a Protocol on Phyto-sanitary regulations governing the import of Canola from Canada to Pakistan. The Protocol was signed by the Deputy Prime Minister and the Canadian Foreign Minister from their respective sides. Video

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 and Canada's Minister of Foreign Affairs, H.E. Anita Anand @AnitaAnandMP, signed the Protocol on the Phytosanitary Import Requirements for Genetically Modified Canola Intended for Food, Feed and Processing (FFP) from Canada to Pakistan at the Prime Minister's Office. The signing ceremony was witnessed by Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif @CMShehbaz. The Protocol establishes the phytosanitary import requirements for Canadian genetically modified canola intended for food, feed and processing and reflects the shared commitment of Pakistan and Canada to strengthening bilateral cooperation in agriculture and trade.

If social media posts of Judge Hamayoun Dilawar are authentic (Tosha Khana Case Judge), this is alarming and raises serious and reasonable doubts on credibility of trial being conducted by him. In my view, propriety demands that he should immediately recuse or disassociate himself from the case. It needs to be noted that Seven Member Bench of the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Malik Qayyum Case (reported in 2001 PLD SC 568) held that bias on part of the judge vitiates judicial proceedings. The court further held that an accused has a right of a fair trial by a judicial minded person, not by someone functioning under an influence or bias as the same paralyses his judicial faculties to conduct fair trial. Bias would vitiate judicial proceedings if such circumstances exist. Bias robs the judge of the confidence that a litigant may have in the judge. Court further held that bias is mental disposition or attitude towards a particular person and covers all kind of hostilities and prejudices against him.

#DidYouKnow that Manipur celebrates the #RathYatra, locally known as ‘Kang Chingba’? The annual chariot festival is marked by great devotion & splendour as it begins at the Shri Govindaji Temple in Imphal, where devotees gather to offer special prayers before joining the grand ceremonial procession. The festival, celebrated amidst the sounds of cymbals & chants, has been an integral part of Manipur’s cultural & religious heritage since 1832. Beautifully blending Vaishnavite traditions with indigenous Meitei customs, it attracts devotees from all over the country to participate in the 10-day celebration, which concludes with ‘Kang Len’ or Poornayatra, marking the ceremonial return of Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra, and Devi Subhadra to their traditional abode. The Government of India is implementing the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) as a flagship initiative to ensure the safety, dignity and social security of sanitation workers while accelerating the transition towards mechanised sanitation across the country. Jointly implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, the scheme aims to eliminate hazardous manual cleaning of sewers and septic tanks by promoting mechanised cleaning practices, skill development and comprehensive welfare measures for sanitation workers. Highlighting the Government's commitment to the welfare of sanitation workers, Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar said that the NAMASTE Scheme reflects the Government's unwavering commitment to ensuring that every sanitation worker is able to work with dignity, safety and social security. Appreciating his contribution to promoting Nepal's adventure tourism, the Hon. Heads of the United Nations Agencies based in Kathmandu paid a joint courtesy call on Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr Shisir Khanal at the Ministry today. The United Nations Resident Coordinator and the Heads of UNDP, WFP, UNESCO, UNODC, UNRCPD, UNICEF, UNFPA and WHO were present for the joint call on. Hon. Foreign Minister reaffirmed Nepal's unwavering commitment to the United Nations as well as a strong and inclusive multilateral system. He appreciated the UN's longstanding partnership in advancing Nepal's journey to development and prosperity and called for an enhanced level of cooperation in the days ahead. Hon. Minister Khanal further underscored the Government's priorities of strengthening good governance, accelerating economic transformation, creating employment opportunities, and harnessing the demographic dividend to achieve sustainable, inclusive and resilient development. On the occasion, the Heads of the UN agencies highlighted the ongoing cooperation between the UN Agencies and Nepal, reiterated their support for Nepal's national priorities and expressed commitment to further strengthening Nepal-UN partnership.

*MESSAGE FROM THE CARIBBEAN COMMUNITY (CARICOM) ON THE CAPSIZING OF THE MV BARIMA IN GUYANA* The Caribbean Community (CARICOM) is deeply saddened by the capsizing of the passenger ferry, MV Barima, off the Atlantic coast near the Pomeroon River. The Community continues to closely follow the ongoing search and rescue operation to account for the passengers and crew. We extend our prayers and support to the families anxiously awaiting news of their loved ones. CARICOM pays tribute to the courage, dedication and selfless efforts of the rescue teams and all who are responding in the aftermath of the incident, led by relevant arms of the Government of Guyana, and including private vessel operators, who mobilized overnight in challenging conditions to save lives. CARICOM stands in solidarity with the Government and people of Guyana, in particular, the families and communities that are being impacted by this unfolding disaster.

"Who says spreading your wings means flying high? Flying low is also flying," reads a line from Low Flight, a poetry collection by Wang Jibing. The book has earned him the Lu Xun Literary Prize, one of China's top literary honors. But what makes the news particularly striking is that Wang is a food delivery rider. Born in east China's Jiangsu Province, Wang, now 56, left school as a teenager due to his family financial hardship. He took on a variety of jobs – from construction work to running a street stall. He eventually chose to become a delivery rider, not only because it paid better, but also because it allowed him to observe passers-by and the scenery along the way, making it easier to capture inspiration for his writing. He had been posting his poems and essays on social media over the past decade, but they failed to make much of a splash. Then came 2019, when a customer entered the wrong address, causing Wang to miss the delivery window. The customer sneered, "You're this old and still delivering food? How stupid can you be?" After that frustrating experience, he wrote a piece titled "Man in a Hurry." It went viral online, and Wang soon became well-known. He began gathering material for his poetry, interviewing and surveying other delivery riders and drawing inspiration from their stories. In 2024, Low Flight was published. The collection vividly portrays this group of workers – though they are at the bottom of society, they still yearn for a better life. Wang's achievement reflects a broader trend: more and more blue-collar workers in China are carving out a place for themselves in different areas. #TheFaces

اسلام آباد: 20 جولائی، 2026. وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیرِ صدارت پاکستان ریلویز ٹرانسفارمیشن پلان پر پیش رفت کا جائزہ اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ پاکستان ریلویز مسافروں اور مال برداری کے لیے سب سے کم لاگت اور مؤثر ذریعۂ نقل و حمل ہے. جدید اور مؤثر ریلوے نظام ملکی معیشت، تجارت اور علاقائی روابط کے فروغ میں کلیدی کردار ادا کرے گا. پاکستان ریلویز کے بنیادی ڈھانچے کی جدید کاری کا پاکستان کے علاقائی تجارت اور لاجسٹکس ہب کے طور پر کردار میں کلیدی کردار ہوگا. وزیراعظم نے ہدایات دیں کہ ریلوے کے ترقیاتی منصوبوں کو اعلیٰ معیار اور مقررہ مدت کے اندر مکمل کیا جائے اور مین ریلوے لائین ون کے روہڑی-ملتان سیکشن کی اپ گریڈیشن کے حوالےسے تجاویز پیش کی جائیں. اجلاس کو ایم ایل-1 اور ایم ایل-3 اپ گریڈیشن، تھر کول ریلوے کنیکٹیویٹی اور دیگر منصوبوں کی پیشرفت پر بریفنگ دی گئی. بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ ایم ایل-1 کی کراچی۔روہڑی سیکشن کے لیے تفصیلی انجینئرنگ ڈیزائن مکمل کر لی گئی ہے. ایم ایل 3 روہڑی-نوکنڈی کی اپ گریڈیشن پی ایس ڈی پی اور برج فنانسنگ تحت کی جائے گی. تھر کول ریل کنینٹیویٹی منصوبے کا 112 کلومیٹر طویل ریلوے ٹریک تھر کول تا چھور ریلوے اسٹیشن پر 60 فیصد کام ہو چکا اور یہ منصوبہ دسمبر 2026 تک مکمل کر لیا جائے گا. بریفنگ میں مزید بتایا گیا کہ وزیراعظم کی ہدایت پر ریلوے کی اصلاحات کے لئے بین الاقوامی کنسلٹنٹ کی خدمات حاصل کر لی گئی ہیں. ریلوے کے ماتحت اسکول اور ہسپتالوں کی سروسز کو آوٹ سورس کیا جا چکا ہے، جبکہ چھ بڑے ریلوے اسٹیشنوں کی کمرشلائزیشن پر کام کا آغاز کیا جا رہا ہے. اجلاس میں وفاقی منصوبہ بندی احسن اقبال، وفاقی وزیر اقتصادی امور احد خان چیمہ، وفاقی وزیر ریلوے حنیف عباسی، وفاقی وزیر انفارمیشن ٹیکنالوجی و ٹیلی کام شزا فاطمہ، مشیر وزیر اعظم برائے نجکاری محمد علی، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ و ریلوے بلال اظہر کیانی اور متعلقہ اعلیٰ سرکاری افسران نے شرکت کی۔ Video

Today's Ramsar Spotlight takes us to Ashtamudi Wetland in Kerala. The name "Ashtamudi" means "eight coned" in Malayalam, referring to the estuary's intricate network of waterways. Over centuries, the historic port city of Kollam on its banks welcomed traders from Persia, China and Europe, shaping a rich cultural landscape. Today, the wetland comes alive each November during the President's Trophy Boat Race, when traditional Chundan Vallams (snake boats) transform its tranquil waters into a vibrant racecourse. #WetlandsofIndia

The World Heritage Site of Dholavira stands as one of the finest examples of the urban ingenuity of Ancient Bharat during 3000-1500 BCE. Its systematically planned layout, advanced water conservation system, humongous reservoirs, elaborately crafted gateways and fortification and large cache of fine artefacts reflect an extraordinary level of engineering and town planning achieved over four and a half millennia ago. Excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) between 1989 and 2005, Dholavira has revealed invaluable insights into one of the world’s earliest urban settlements. Today, this remarkable site continues to inspire scholars and visitors alike, showcasing the innovation, resilience, and architectural excellence of India’s ancient past. Video

India once clothed the world, accounting for a quarter of global economic output in 1700. Today, its share of global apparel exports sits at around 3%, roughly where it has stagnated for two decades even as Bangladesh's rose from 2.2% to 9% and Vietnam's from 1% to 6%. In their recent op-ed in @IndianExpress & @FinancialXpress, Prof. Ashok Gulati (@agulati115), Distinguished Professor at ICRIER, and Dr. Sulakshana Rao, Senior Fellow at ICRIER, ask what it will take for India to raise its apparel export share in a $521-billion global apparel market. Drawing on their new book, Stitching India's Apparel Export Strategy: From Farm to Foreign, they lay out an ecosystem approach to competitiveness built on five pillars: scale and ecosystem, capital, labour and skilling, clusters and institutions, and market access and trade facilitation. The piece examines the "missing middle" of mid-sized export-ready firms, the need to expand the apparel manufacturing to labour abundant regions like central and eastern India, the cotton-skewed fibre mix that sits out of step with a man-made-fibre-dominated global market, and how initiatives like PM-MITRA and recent FTAs with the UK and EU could help reposition India as a scale-driven, sustainable global sourcing hub. Some votes a national party just can't buy. The BJP is learning this the hard way in UP. Start with who the Kurmis are. - UP's second-largest OBC group after the Yadavs, about 7 to 10% of the state. - Packed tightly enough to decide 30 to 40 seats. - Backed the NDA for 10 years. - NDA's Kurmi vote has slid from 80% in 2019 to 66% in 2022 to 61% in 2024. You can see it in who got elected too. UP sent 11 Kurmi MPs to Parliament in 2024. Seven were from the Samajwadi Party. Only three were from the BJP. Here's the odd part. The BJP has an ally, Anupriya Patel's Apna Dal, whose whole job is to hold the Kurmi vote for it. The vote is leaving anyway. Why? Because the SP did something the BJP structurally couldn't. - SP let local Kurmi leaders build their own following. - It picked up district-level leaders from the BSP, gave them tickets, and ran them straight at the BJP. - In three seats it put up a Kurmi against a BJP Brahmin. It won all three. The BJP can't copy this easily. It's a national party with a fixed ideology. It won't bend to one caste, and it won't let a local leader grow into his own power centre. As one BJP leader put it – Kurmis follow their caste leaders, not a party. And the BJP makes it hard for such a leader to rise from inside. That's what the ally, Apna Dal, was for. But it only delivers around Mirzapur. Even there, Anupriya Patel's own win margin crashed from 2.3 lakh votes in 2019 to 38,000 in 2024. And now the ally is walking away from its own job. After some internal splits, Apna Dal has made a Dalit its state chief and told workers to stop being a Kurmi-only party. So the BJP did what national parties do. It fixed things from the top. نزدیک به پنج سال پس از بازگشت طالبان به قدرت در اسد ۱۴۰۰، ساختار اقتصادی افغانستان دستخوش تغییرات گسترده‌ای شده است. در میان نهادهایی که در این دوره جایگاه ویژه‌ای یافته‌اند، شرکت انکشاف ملی به‌عنوان بازوی اصلی اجرای پروژه‌های عمرانی حکومت، به یکی از مهم‌ترین بازیگران اقتصادی کشور تبدیل شده است. این شرکت که از ادغام چندین تصدی بزرگ دولتی شکل گرفته، امروز بخش قابل‌توجهی از فعالیت‌های ساختمانی، تولید مصالح و اجرای پروژه‌های زیربنایی را در اختیار دارد و عملا به یکی از بزرگ‌ترین مجموعه‌های اقتصادی وابسته به حکومت طالبان بدل شده است. بااین‌حال، روند گزارش‌دهی این شرکت در سال‌های اخیر با ابهام‌هایی همراه بوده است. شرکت انکشاف ملی در سال‌های نخست پس از تغییر نظام، اطلاعات مربوط به پروژه‌ها و وضعیت مالی خود را تا پایان سال ۲۰۲۳ در قالب گزارش‌های رسمی مکتوب منتشر می‌کرد، اما پس از آن، گزارش مالی جدید، ترازنامه یا جزئیات دقیقی درباره‌ی درآمدها، هزینه‌ها و عملکرد اقتصادی آن در دسترس عمومی قرار نگرفته است. این توقف در انتشار اطلاعات، پرسش‌هایی را درباره‌ی میزان شفافیت مالی، نحوه مدیریت منابع و سازوکارهای حساب‌دهی این نهاد بزرگ اقتصادی ایجاد کرده است. آخرین داده‌های مالی منتشرشده از سوی شرکت انکشاف ملی، مربوط به سال ۲۰۲۳، تصویری از ابعاد گسترده‌ی این مجموعه ارائه می‌کند. براساس اطلاعات رسمی منتشرشده در وب‌سایت این شرکت، ارزش دارایی‌های منقول و غیرمنقول آن بیش از ۵۴ میلیارد افغانی اعلام شده است. در کنار آن، ارزش مجموعی پروژه‌های تحت مدیریت شرکت به ۱۲۴ میلیارد افغانی می‌رسد؛ پروژه‌هایی که براساس همین گزارش‌ها، ۲۶.۸ میلیارد افغانی عواید ناخالص و ۱۱ میلیارد افغانی سود خالص ایجاد کرده‌اند. همچنین این شرکت حدود ۱۷.۵ میلیارد افغانی از وزارت‌خانه‌ها طلبکار اعلام شده است. ارزش پروژه‌های تحت مدیریت این شرکت، معادل نزدیک به یک‌چهارم بودجه‌ی عمومی سالانه‌ی افغانستان در سال‌های اخیر است. تنها دارایی‌های ثبت‌شده‌ی آن از بودجه‌ی انکشافی بسیاری از سال‌های حکومت پیشین نیز بیشتر است و سود خالص ۱۱ میلیارد افغانی آن با بودجه‌ی سالانه چندین وزارت‌خانه متوسط دولتی برابری می‌کند. این ارقام، که آخرین تصویر رسمی از وضعیت مالی شرکت پیش از توقف گزارش‌دهی عمومی به شمار می‌روند، ابعاد اقتصادی نهادی را نشان می‌دهند که در کم‌تر از چند سال به یکی از بزرگ‌ترین مراکز مدیریت دارایی و پروژه‌های حکومتی طالبان تبدیل شده است. بیشتر بخوانید: etilaatroz.com/257645

#ChinaSeen Nestled in the deserts of northwest China's Gansu Province, the #UNESCO World Heritage Mogao Caves are the world's largest and best-preserved Buddhist cave art site, with a collection of 735 caves spanning a cliff face 1,700 meters long. Among them are 492 caves housing paintings and sculptures dating back to the 4th century AD. Adorned with intricate murals, sculptures and architectural designs, they bear witness to the dynamic cultural exchanges along the Silk Road. The construction of the #MogaoCaves is generally believed to have begun sometime in the 4th century AD, when they served as places of Buddhist meditation for hermit monks. The caves continued to be expanded until the 14th century, eventually becoming places of worship and pilgrimage for the public. The Mogao Caves, an unparalleled treasure trove of ancient art, offer invaluable insight into the evolution of Chinese art, religious beliefs and daily life over the course of a millennium. Along with the Longmen Grottoes and the Yungang Grottoes, they are one of the three great ancient Buddhist sculptural sites in China. (Photos via VCG and IC) #ChinaTravel #CivilizationsShine

Ball (@deanwball) Some observations on Kimi: 1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run. 2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China. 3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "the art of not being governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex. 4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure." This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business. 5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this. 6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/deanwball/status/2078133895766114412#m

I'm a cardiologist. Everyone is sharing this study as a skin story. They're burying the part that matters. Scientists took the aorta of a 75-year-old donor, applied a single engineered enzyme, and stripped away more than 70% of the molecular damage — bringing it down to the levels you'd see in a 30-year-old artery. Published five days ago in Nature Communications. Revel Pharmaceuticals, with Calico and the University of Colorado. Here's what they erased. Sugar reacts with proteins in your body the same way heat browns bread — slowly, over a lifetime. It leaves behind a residue called CML, the most abundant advanced glycation end product in aging tissue. It welds itself onto collagen and elastin in your skin, your eye lens, and your arterial walls. Two things follow. Your arteries stiffen. And CML latches onto a receptor called RAGE, which drives chronic inflammation — the exact fire I've been writing about for months as the engine of heart disease. Since the 1980s this damage was considered permanent. Your body has no enzyme to remove it. Every existing approach only slows new damage from forming. Nothing touched what was already there. So they built an enzyme that doesn't exist in nature. They screened 45,000 protein structures, then ran five rounds of directed evolution across more than 500 million variants until they had CMLase — a molecular lawnmower that oxidizes the CML off the protein and restores the original, healthy lysine underneath. Not patched. Reversed. Over 70% cleared from elderly arterial tissue. Over 55% from elderly skin — below the levels found in 31-year-old skin. 45-78% in lens proteins. The CEO said they expected 20% and were floored. Arterial stiffness drives systolic hypertension, heart failure, and stroke, and I have no drug that reverses it. I can slow the process. I cannot undo it. This paper says undoing it may be possible. The caveats are real and I won't skip them. This was done on donated tissue in a dish, not in a living person. No functional data yet — we don't know if that artery got measurably more elastic. Delivering a large enzyme deep into human tissue is a hard, unsolved problem. Clinical trials are years away. But something considered permanent for forty years just came off human tissue. We spent a century learning to slow aging. Someone finally figured out how to erase it. Thank you @theallinpod @friedberg @chamath @pesottas The All-In Podcast (@theallinpod) Friedberg: New study shows enzyme reverses skin age from 70+ years to 31 Chamath: That’s a $2T market. Did Scientists Just Discover How to Reverse Skin Aging!? “CML is kind of the predominant molecule that gets formed in this extracellular matrix that's driving aging, and nothing breaks it down. So these scientists set out to try and create an enzyme, an enzyme is a protein that breaks something down, that can break down CML. And so these guys kind of went out and they took the target, which is CML, and tried to figure out, ‘Okay, how do we actually degrade CML, clear that extracellular matrix, and reverse aging?’ They started to test it on the proteins that we would find in our body, casein, collagen, retinal proteins, which are in your eye, hemoglobin, and they were able to get rid of 52 to 97% of the CML, just degrade it away. And then they found several sites where they were able to degrade over 90%. And then they took actual human skin from elderly patients that had donated their skin, and they put this enzyme onto that skin, and they were able to eliminate 55% of the CML on the skin, basically reverse the skin's age down to the age of a 31-year-old, this is from greater than 70-year-old patients, just by putting this enzyme on the skin. And so it's kind of a groundbreaking demonstration of combination of AlphaFold, what's called directed evolution, where you change the order of the DNA that changes the structure of the protein to test different proteins, do high throughput screening, and ultimately make a novel protein that doesn't exist in nature today that can do something pretty profound for human health.” Chamath: “It will be a trillion-dollar market. If you can create a cream…” Friedberg: “I mean, dude, if you could put this enzyme literally on your skin and have it absorb in…” Chamath: “Game over. That alone is $2 trillion.” Video — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/theallinpod/status/2078334237481046412#m

Trump Gives Green Light to Saudi Nuclear Program The Donald Trump administration has finalized the draft of a bilateral nuclear agreement that authorizes Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium on its own territory. Although the negotiating teams have completed the terms, the document still awaits Trump’s final signature and approval by the U.S. Congress. This framework breaks with the region’s long-standing non-proliferation rules. Unlike the deal with the United Arab Emirates, which permanently renounced uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing while accepting strict IAEA inspections, the agreement with the Saudis does not require Riyadh to adopt the Agency’s inspection regime. Oversight will be limited to a bilateral pact between the United States and Saudi Arabia. This reinforces what Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has already said openly: if Iran gets a nuclear weapon, Saudi Arabia will want one too. It sounds like a clear signal that Riyadh believes Tehran already has, or is very close to having, the bomb, which explains the intense pressure they are putting on Washington. The situation puts the U.S. in a complicated position. Saudi Arabia’s ballistic missile program is developed in partnership with China, complete with technology transfers. If the Americans don’t give in now, the Saudis have plenty of money to look for other partners. This is not just about civilian nuclear energy. For that, it would be enough to buy reactors and import ready-made fuel. What Riyadh really wants is to master the full nuclear fuel cycle, especially domestic uranium enrichment. With this infrastructure, Saudi Arabia is building a nuclear latency capability: it will control the core technology needed to develop a weapon in relatively short order if pushed by an existential threat. Weekend Ukraine map thread for Sunday 19th July 2026 Another focus on Crimea this weekend. Unmanned Systems have disabled much of the ferries operating across the strait, leaving two larger ferries being towed from Kavkaz to get supplies to the peninsula. Of course, a large amount of supply still arrives via the bridge disguised, but this is where we are with the heavy goods. Shipping in the Black Sea has been further disrupted with long range Firepoint strikes in the ringed area. The vessels have now dispersed from the anchorages, and are harder to strike but the damage has been done. Strikes here should settle down, similar to how the Sea of Azov strikes have settled due to a lack of targets. There are hundreds of new additions, we can only feature a few in the thread below. The full strikes can be seen on the map link in our bio. It is not just Crimea, there are strikes across the occupied territories from Mariupol to Luhansk. It is much more important than any political machinations going on right now. Elsewhere, there is not much to report that's actually changed land wise on the front. If you'd like us to give a focus on any specific area for you, please let us know. Russian strikes on Kyiv continue, and Russian strikes on Ukrainian shipping continue, so the Black Sea will likely not be useful for either side soon, a deal Ukraine is more than happy to make.

Islamabad: 14 July 2026. Ms. Michelle Bachelet, candidate for the position of the UN Secretary General, called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif at the Prime Minister House in Islamabad today. Deputy Prime Minister & Foreign Minister Sen. Muhammad Ishaq Dar and Foreign Secretary Amb. Amna Baloch were also present. While welcoming Ms. Bachelet to Pakistan, the Prime Minister reiterated Pakistan’s strong support for strengthening multilateralism as well as for ensuring the central role of the United Nations in addressing global challenges. The Prime Minister called for upholding the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations, faithful implementation of the UN resolutions and international treaties, as well as for achieving balanced progress across all three pillars of the United Nations - peace and security, development, and human rights. He also called for enhanced international cooperation and increased focus on accelerating the implementation of the global development agenda. Ms. Bachelet commended Pakistan's historic and invaluable contributions to the United Nations, and appreciated the country's ongoing contributions to regional and international peace and security. Argue what you will about the ability for Iran to close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, the irrefutable reality is that they can absolutely devastate Gulf energy and water infrastructure. One cannot reasonable assert otherwise. There is zero evidence whatsoever to support that the Iranian people are "so close" to rising up and toppling the regime. It failed miserably in January due to insufficient numbers, insufficient planning and coordination, and insufficient arming. Now, we've rallied Iran around the flag by bombing schoolchildren in Minab, threatening to wipe out their entire civilization, and a plethora of other missteps. No person without an insane degree of ideological extremism would say the Iranian regime has LESS support now than they did prior to the conflict. That is utterly absurd. The Iranian's have a FAR greater pain tolerance than the rest of the global economy does. This is an existential war for them, and an entirely optional war for the United States, and completely against the will of the rest of the world. We can not reopen the Strait of Hormuz through military power. We have tried this extensively through bombing campaigns and naval coordination via the Omani Route. We simply can not protect these vessels. These are the undeniable fundamentals of this conflict. They cannot rationally be argued against, nor are they remotely controversial. The FUNDAMENTALS show that continuing this escalation spiral is incredibly foolish for President Trump.

VIDEO | Delhi: Reacting to Rohit Sharma's 138-run knock at Lord's, his childhood coach Dinesh Lad says, "Two days ago, I spoke to him. I told him that I want to see him playing in the 2027 ODI World Cup, and I was confident that he would be there. Today, he showed everyone what he is capable of. There has been a lot of criticism that Rohit Sharma should retire-that he has done enough and that his time is over. I never agreed with that criticism. I always believed in his ability, and today he answered all his critics with his performance. The way he paced and constructed his innings today showed his experience, temperament and class. In my opinion, he has once again established himself as a strong contender to represent India in the 2027 ODI World Cup. Critics will always continue to criticise, but such things do not affect him. He remains focused on his cricket and on contributing to the team. He has already won the T20 World Cup and the Champions Trophy for India. One thing that has always stayed with him is the disappointment of missing out on the 2011 ODI World Cup squad and the heartbreak of India falling short in the 2023 ODI World Cup final. Ever since then, his biggest dream has been to win the 50-over World Cup for India. If India wants to lift the ODI World Cup next year, Rohit is a must-have in the team." Pakistani media have reported that transit trade between Afghanistan and Pakistan fell to its lowest level in Pakistan's 2026 fiscal year, with its value dropping to just $367 million. According to the report, before 2021, transit trade between the two countries was worth around $5 billion, with approximately 89,000 containers transported annually. This year, however, the number of containers declined to about 11,600. The report noted that transit trade was at a strong level in 2023, when the number of containers exceeded 102,000 and the total trade value reached $6.7 billion. It said Afghanistan's shift toward Iran as an alternative transit route, along with the closure of crossings between Kabul and Islamabad, were among the main reasons for the sharp decline. The report further added that Afghanistan had already begun reducing its reliance on transit trade through Pakistan even before the crossings' closure, while seeking to expand trade and transit links with Iran and the Central Asian countries. #TOLOnews_English

Félix Plasencia. DPM/FM extended his warm congratulations to Minister Plasencia on his appointment. He conveyed Pakistan’s heartfelt condolences over the devastating earthquakes that recently struck Venezuela. He reaffirmed Pakistan’s unwavering solidarity with the Government and the people of Venezuela during this difficult time and expressed confidence in their resilience and recovery. Minister Plasencia thanked DPM/FM for Pakistan’s message of sympathy and solidarity. He also expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s support and humanitarian solidarity with the victims of the natural disasters, underscoring the importance of mutual support in times of need. He further acknowledged Pakistan’s constructive role in promoting dialogue and de-escalation in the regional situation involving the United States and Iran and commended its commitment to peace and diplomacy. The two Ministers exchanged views on the longstanding friendly relations between Pakistan and Venezuela and reaffirmed their shared commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties. They discussed opportunities to expand cooperation across a broad range of sectors, including trade, investment, business, agriculture, IT, and other areas of mutual interest. Both sides underscored the considerable potential for enhancing economic collaboration and fostering stronger people-to-people contacts for the mutual benefit of the two countries. DPM/FM emphasized the importance of sustained high-level engagement to reinvigorate bilateral relations and further deepen cooperation. Both sides appreciated the continued close coordination between Pakistan and Venezuela at multilateral forums on issues of common interest. They agreed to remain in close contact and to meet at the earliest appropriate opportunity. @Cancilleria_ve

Mufti Taqi Usmani has declared purchasing goods with cryptocurrency “impermissible”, citing research conducted by experts so far which found that cryptocurrency does not qualify as “wealth”. The fatwa was originally issued by Darul Ifta, Jamia Darul Uloom, Karachi, and dated 24 Zilhaj 1447 AH (June 10, 2026). I don’t know which experts but I am not aware of any individuals in Pakistan, who are known as experts on cryptocurrencies, which is a fast evolving financial product. Leaving aside this issue of competence, I believe some important questions need to be asked about Mufti Taqi Usmani's public role and legacy. Mufti Taqi Usmani's judicial career began during General Zia-ul-Haq's military dictatorship. In 1982, he was appointed by Zia to the Federal Shariat Court, at a time when Pakistan was under martial law and democratic institutions had been weakened. To understand the significance of that appointment, one must understand the politics of the Zia era. Islamization was not merely a programme of legal reform; it became a central source of legitimacy for a military government that had seized power through a coup and removed an elected prime minister through what has now been established as judicial murder. Religious laws, institutions, and symbolism became closely intertwined with the state's political project. This process fundamentally reshaped Pakistan's legal and social landscape, and its consequences remain the subject of intense debate. The Federal Shariat Court was established within this broader context as a key institution for reviewing laws against Islamic injunctions. Appointments to the court were therefore not simply routine judicial appointments; they were part of a wider transformation of Pakistan's legal order. Mufti Taqi Usmani's role in that transformation deserves examination not because he was a religious scholar, but because he occupied a position of significant judicial authority at a historically consequential moment. Some of his judgments also had major economic and social implications. A prominent example is the Qazalbash Waqf case, decided by the Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court in 1989, in which Mufti Taqi Usmani authored the majority opinion. The judgment held that key aspects of Pakistan's land reform framework, particularly restrictions on land ownership, were inconsistent with Islamic principles. The significance of this judgment was highlighted by senior lawyer Abid Hasan Minto, former President of the Supreme Court Bar Association, who argued that the issue was not merely about property rights but about the structure of economic and political power in Pakistan. He placed the decision in the context of Pakistan's long-standing agrarian inequality and the continued influence of large landholders, arguing that weakening land reform efforts had consequences far beyond a legal dispute. For critics, therefore, the Qazalbash Waqf judgment was not simply a matter of interpreting religious principles; it was a decision with profound implications for Pakistan's social structure, rural inequality, and the concentration of political power among large landholding elites. Supporters viewed the decision as a defence of private property rights. Critics argued that it weakened attempts to address Pakistan's highly unequal agrarian structure and protected the interests of large landholders. This remains an important debate because land ownership has shaped Pakistan's economic inequality and political power for generations. The second issue is Islamic banking. Mufti Taqi Usmani has been one of the most influential figures in the development and certification of modern Islamic finance. Through his association with institutions including Meezan Bank and other Islamic financial entities, he has played a major role in shaping an industry that has become a significant part of Pakistan's banking sector. However, Islamic banking itself deserves serious scrutiny and debate. This criticism is not limited to religious critics. Former finance minister Dr Miftah Ismail recently argued that much of modern Islamic banking has become "more in nomenclature and less in substance." He questioned whether many products genuinely reflect the principles of risk-sharing and partnership that Islamic finance originally promised, or whether they often replicate conventional banking outcomes through different contractual structures. This debate is not about faith. It is about whether practical outcomes match stated principles. When religious scholars play central roles in approving financial products and providing Shariah certification to commercial institutions, questions about governance and transparency are entirely legitimate. What advisory roles exist? What compensation arrangements are in place? What disclosure standards apply? How are potential conflicts of interest managed? How independent can oversight be when the institutions being overseen provide compensation for that oversight? These are not accusations. They are normal questions of corporate governance, particularly where publicly listed institutions are involved. Indeed, if Islamic finance claims to represent a higher ethical standard than conventional finance, then transparency and accountability should be its defining characteristics. My concern is not with religious belief. It is with power without accountability. No one — whether a politician, general, judge, banker, academic, or religious scholar — should be beyond scrutiny. Respect for scholarship does not require intellectual submission. Religious credentials do not create immunity from questions. Public influence brings public responsibility. And the uncomfortable questions are often the ones that matter most.

EL MUNDIAL DE LAS APUESTAS: DURANTE EL TORNEO, LOS “MERCADOS DE PREDICCIÓN” MOVILIZARON MÁS DE USD 50 MIL MILLONES Kalshi, Polymarket y Rothera concentraron enormes sumas en operaciones ligadas al torneo, disputando terreno a las casas de juego tradicionales, que también reportaron cifras récord El Mundial 2026 dejó una marca que va más allá del resultado deportivo. De acuerdo con un relevamiento publicado por CoinDesk, las plataformas de mercados de predicción se convirtieron en uno de los protagonistas económicos del torneo, con volúmenes de negociación que rivalizaron e incluso superaron a los de las casas de apuestas deportivas tradicionales en Estados Unidos. Kalshi, una de las plataformas más activas del sector, alcanzó en junio un volumen nominal total de 31.000 millones de dólares, un salto de más del 70% respecto de mayo. Según datos de la firma de análisis Dune citados por el medio, los contratos vinculados al deporte representaron cerca del 85% de esa negociación. La empresa precisó además que el volumen específico asociado al Mundial en su plataforma llegó a 22.420 millones de dólares. El resto del sector también mostró cifras elevadas. Polymarket, el exchange internacional de mercados de predicción, marcó un récord mensual con 10.800 millones de dólares negociados, mientras que su versión regulada para el mercado estadounidense sumó otros 3.500 millones, casi el doble de lo registrado en mayo. A ese panorama se sumó Rothera, la plataforma lanzada en junio por Robinhood y Susquehanna International Group, que en su primer mes de operación procesó 2.000 millones de dólares y ya concentra el 7% del mercado de predicciones en Estados Unidos, según estimaciones de Bank of America difundidas por CoinDesk. 🔗infob.ae/4fc1STk

Homes have disappeared under water, families have been displaced, and lives have been lost. Yet, based on the reported relief allocation, it amounts to roughly 28 taka per affected person—an amount that has drawn widespread criticism. For flood survivors, relief isn’t just a number. It’s food, clean water, medicine, shelter, and the chance to rebuild. Disaster response should be judged not by promises, but by how quickly and effectively help reaches those who need it most. An outreach programme on the Income Tax Act, 2025, Income Tax Rules, 2026, and TDS-related issues was organised today at DRDO Bhawan by the Directorate of Management & Security (DMS), DRDO. The programme commenced with an address by Dr. Ravindra Singh, DG (R&M), who highlighted the importance of awareness and compliance with the latest income tax provisions. The technical sessions were delivered by Ms. Beenu, Additional Commissioner of Income Tax; Shri Y. N. Saxena, Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax; and the team from Aaykar Bhawan, New Delhi who provided detailed insights into the provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025, Income Tax Rules, 2026, and TDS-related issues while addressing participants' queries. The interactive sessions enhanced participants understanding of the new tax framework and strengthened statutory compliance among DDOs and PAOs across DRDO. The programme concluded with a Vote of Thanks by the Director DMS.

Competition between US and Chinese AI models is heating up: The proportion of tokens used by US firms that run through Chinese AI models on OpenRouter is up to a record ~58%. OpenRouter is a platform that allows developers and companies to access and compare AI models from multiple providers, making it a useful gauge of real-world AI model adoption. This percentage has TRIPLED since mid-January, overtaking American peers on the platform for the first time in March. The token share of Chinese models briefly rose as high as 63% in the first week of July. By comparison, Chinese models accounted for less than 10% of usage at the start of 2025, while US models accounted for ~80%. DeepSeek has emerged as the most popular choice among American firms in recent months. Chinese AI models are rapidly gaining market share.

“Hermanos para siempre” 🥹 Antonio Banderas (@antoniobanderas) Hola amigos. Hoy es la final del Campeonato del Mundo de Fútbol. Naturalmente quiero que gane España, pero también el fútbol y todo aquello que une a nuestros dos países. Durante un rato España y Argentina serán rivales. Después volverán a ser lo que siempre han sido para mí: dos pueblos hermanos. Quizá suene tonto decir esto, pero siento la necesidad de expresar que, pase lo que pase, yo seguiré admirando a los inmensos artistas argentinos con los que he tenido el privilegio de trabajar, seguiré admirando a sus jugadores de fútbol y, por supuesto, seguiré queriendo a mis muchos amigos de Argentina y a todo un país al que me siento profundamente unido. El deporte tiene esa maravillosa capacidad de enfrentarnos sin dividirnos, de competir sin dejar de respetarnos y de recordarnos que la verdadera victoria nunca debería pertenecer al odio, sino a la admiración. Que gane quien mejor juegue. Y que, cuando el árbitro señale el final, celebremos todos algo mucho más importante que un resultado: la amistad entre dos países que hablan el mismo idioma, y la oportunidad que nos da la vida para con el buen comportamiento de jugadores e hinchas, de dar ejemplo, de enorgullecer y hacer brillar a las comunidades hispanas de todo el mundo. "The economic effects of illegal migration has been disastrous to poor people in this country." Of course, Alex Karp and anyone who understands economics knows this to be true. Two examples this week. 1. Was talking to a small builder. Was complaining about his backlog because, "A few months ago ICE started picking up my framers and I'm having trouble hiring." I told him about how in the '80s I had friends who, as 16, 17, and 18+ made money in summer working as framers. His response, "They are too few and cost too much." Of course they do: there has not been a demand signal for a long time, and illegal labor undercuts legal labor. 2. This is more personal. A few month ago, we decided that we needed to get the concrete driveway replaced with pavers. Knew a guy and told him we would be ready in June. When we touched base with him, he said, "I can't. ICE took my work crew..." I had no idea he hired illegals. We decided to go with him because he did good work, and bid lower than the other company we got a quote from. With his, "I don't know when I can hire new help..." issue, We called the other company, and as I have done other business with them in the past, originally was backlogged until the fall, but had a cancellation, put us at the top of the list, and will start next week. श्री विवेक अग्रवाल, सचिव, संस्कृति मंत्रालय ने आज राष्ट्रीय पुस्तकालय, बेलवेडियर में भारत के प्रथम ‘शब्द संग्रहालय’ के लोकार्पण समारोह में स्वागत संबोधन के दौरान कहा कि यह संग्रहालय माननीय प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi के विजन के अनुरूप स्थापित किया गया है। संग्रहालय में ध्वनि से शब्द, शब्द से भाषा और भाषा से लिपि के विकास की यात्रा तथा ब्राह्मी और खरोष्ठी जैसी प्राचीन लिपियों के वैश्विक प्रभाव को प्रदर्शित किया गया है। साथ ही, इस दौरान श्री अग्रवाल ने यह भी जानकारी साझा की कि संस्कृति मंत्रालय द्वारा ‘ज्ञान भारतम मिशन’ के अंतर्गत अब तक 1 करोड़ 18 लाख से अधिक पांडुलिपियों की पहचान की जा चुकी है और उनके डिजिटलीकरण का कार्य जारी है। संस्कृति सचिव ज्ञान भारतम के महत्त्व को रेखांकित करते हुए कहते हैं कि ‘ज्ञान भारतम’ इस संग्रहालय की वास्तविक आत्मा और मूल भावना है। उन्होंने विश्वास व्यक्त किया कि ‘शब्द संग्रहालय’ के प्रथम चरण की यह शुरुआत ‘ज्ञान भारतम’ के माध्यम से भारत की ज्ञान परंपरा को और अधिक प्रभावी ढंग से आगे बढ़ाने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाएगी। #MuseumOfWord #CultureUnitesAll Video

Dr. Joram Aniya, Member, NITI Aayog, called on Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, during her visit to the State to discuss key priorities for sustainable development, and long-term growth. The discussions focused on enhancing disaster preparedness and resilient infrastructure while exploring collaboration in school education, tourism, culture, youth affairs, and sports. Emphasis was laid on integrating disaster risk reduction into development planning and addressing the unique geographical and climatic challenges of the North Eastern States. Dr. Joram Aniya also proposed organising a National Workshop on Sustainable Tourism in Arunachal Pradesh in November 2026 to promote community-based tourism, showcase the State’s rich cultural and natural heritage, and unlock new avenues for sustainable economic growth. Shri Pema Khandu welcomed the proposal and appreciated the continued support of NITI Aayog and NDMA in advancing a resilient and sustainable Arunachal Pradesh in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. #ArunachalPradesh #DisasterResilience @PMOIndia @narendramodi @Rao_InderjitS @MIB_India @PIB_India @DDNewslive @ashoklahiribjp

स्टार्टअप इंडिया मिशन: सपनों से सफलता तक, भारत की नई उड़ान...🚀🇮🇳 एक समय था जब साल 2014 से पहले देश का युवा सिर्फ नौकरी पाने का सपना देखता था। प्रतिभा थी, विचार थे, लेकिन उन्हें आगे बढ़ाने के लिए न पूंजी थी, न अनुकूल नीतियां और न ही ऐसा माहौल जो उद्यमिता को प्रोत्साहित कर सके। लेकिन साल 2014 में श्री @narendramodi के प्रधानमंत्री बनने के बाद भारत ने एक नई सोच अपनाई— "अब युवा केवल Job Seekers नहीं, बल्कि Job Creators भी बनेंगे।" इसी सोच को साकार करने के लिए 16 जनवरी 2016 को शुरू हुआ स्टार्टअप इंडिया मिशन, जिसने भारत में उद्यमिता की तस्वीर बदल दी। आज की ये उपलब्धियां बताती हैं कि यह बदलाव कितना बड़ा है- ✅ 2.23 लाख+ DPIIT मान्यता प्राप्त स्टार्टअप्स ✅ 23.36 लाख+ प्रत्यक्ष रोजगार का सृजन ✅ 10,000 करोड़ रुपये का Fund of Funds Framework ✅ मजबूत Seed Funding Ecosystem ✅ 1.07 लाख+ स्टार्टअप्स में कम से कम एक महिला निदेशक/साझेदार ✅ Digital India और UPI के माध्यम से मजबूत डिजिटल आधार ✅ भारत दुनिया का तीसरा सबसे बड़ा स्टार्टअप इकोसिस्टम बनने की दिशा में अग्रसर वर्ष 2025-26 भी इस यात्रा का एक महत्वपूर्ण पड़ाव रहा। केवल एक वित्तीय वर्ष में 55,200+ नए स्टार्टअप्स को मान्यता मिली, स्टार्टअप रिकॉग्निशन में 51.6% और प्रत्यक्ष रोजगार में 36.1% की वृद्धि दर्ज की गई। यह केवल आंकड़ों की कहानी नहीं, बल्कि उन लाखों युवाओं की सफलता की कहानी है, जिन्होंने अपने विचारों को उद्यम में बदला, रोजगार के नए अवसर बनाए और भारत को वैश्विक नवाचार के मानचित्र पर नई पहचान दिलाई। आज भारत में स्टार्टअप केवल एक व्यवसाय नहीं, बल्कि आत्मनिर्भर भारत, नवाचार और रोजगार सृजन की मजबूत नींव बन चुके हैं। Video

WSJ: THE SAVE AMERICA ACT BACKFIRE In a floor speech Thursday, North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis argued that even if Congress whooped through the bill, there isn’t time to implement it before November. By his reckoning, the U.S. has about 10,000 county clerks or municipal entities that carry out America’s decentralized elections. The midterms are barely 100 days away, early voting sooner. “The math doesn’t work,” he said. “It can’t be done.” Mr. Tillis isn’t against ID rules, and he helped pass North Carolina’s. “We should figure out a way to get every state to get to voter ID,” he said. Yet he was unsparing toward Congress’s proponents of the SAVE America Act. “Mr. President, these people are misleading you if they’re telling you that this can be implemented by November,” he said. “This seems like a legit proposal, but it isn’t.” Unfortunately, the message from Mr. Trump and others has been that America’s elections can’t be trusted, and the only hope is the SAVE America Act. Aside from being untrue, this is a political backfire for the GOP. If Republican voters believe it, and the bill falls short, then why waste time going to the polls in November? Has the GOP already forgotten how Mr. Trump’s fraud outbursts cost them two Senate seats in the 2021 Georgia runoffs? wsj.com/opinion/donald-trump…

Sandra Joyce, VP Google Threat Intelligence, spent the past year arguing that disrupting adversary infrastructure has to become normal practice. She’s right. January 2026: Google's threat intel team and partners dismantled IPIDEA, the world's largest residential proxy network. Google counted 550+ distinct threat groups using it, including state actors from China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran. Court orders killed the storefronts and 7,400+ C2 servers went dark. Monday July 13, 2026: The EU and UK rolled out their first-ever joint cyber sanctions package against Russia. Scott Jasper’s study of Russian cyber operations says it bluntly: sanctions and indictments have “done little to alter Moscow’s behavior.” You can't freeze assets that were never here. You can't arrest a GRU officer who never leaves Moscow. Sanctioning at that scale is record-keeping, not deterrence. What will actually degrade an adversary? Joyce's point is that the private sector IS the infrastructure adversaries abuse. Private tech companies own the infrastructure, the platforms, apps, and networks, that these attacks run on, and they can shut an operation down directly and immediately. The most useful thing government can do is to build the legal scaffolding that lets the private sector run these operations at scale. My own proposal is more controversial: a licensed cyber letter of marque system (think bounty hunters for cybercrime) requiring congressional authorization, for limited private-sector offensive operations under strict oversight. If you don’t run a hyperscaler, none of this sounds like yours to act on. It is. For defenders who aren't Google: robtlee73.substack.com/p/san… Tell me where you land on this. And would the letter of marque idea go too far for you? I want the argument.

A glimpse into the world of the 'Museum Of Word,' inaugurated in Kolkata on 19th July 2026 by Hon'ble Minister of Home Affairs & Cooperation Shri @AmitShah. Developed by the Ministry of Culture and situated at the historic Belvedere House within the National Library campus, it is India's first immersive language museum and explores the country's rich linguistic & storytelling traditions. The museum features nine interactive galleries equipped with advanced technologies such as hand-gesture sensors, acoustic hallways, and radio frequency identification (RFID) devices. Adding another literary landmark to Kolkata's rich cultural journey! #MuseumsReimagined #CultureUnitesAll Video

Jordanian authorities have evacuated Aqaba's international airport and seaport, and Americans are being urged to avoid both locations. The alert comes after multiple Iranian missile and drone attacks on Jordan in recent days, including strikes on U.S. military facilities, as well as Iranian warnings that countries supporting U.S. military operations could face additional attacks. U.S. Embassy Amman (@USEmbassyJordan) Security Alert: U.S. Embassy Amman - July 19. 2026 Due to a specific and credible threat, Jordanian authorities evacuated the international airport and seaport in Aqaba. We strongly advise all Americans to refrain traveling to either the airport or seaport. Continue to follow all Jordanian authorities’ security directives. U.S. Embassy Amman continues to advise all Americans to avoid travel to military bases in Jordan. On March 2, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members to leave Jordan due to safety risks. Actions to Take: Please visit Jordan’s National Center for Security and Crisis Management website for public safety guidelines, including explanations of emergency sirens in Jordan. Avoid all demonstrations and large gatherings. Avoid all areas where there is a heavy police presence. Monitor local media. Follow the instructions of local authorities. Contact your airline directly for flight change details if your flight is affected. Exercise caution and stay alert at locations publicly associated with the United States. Keep a low profile. Enroll in the Department of State’s Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP). STEP enrollment connects you to the U.S. embassy or consulate so you get the latest security updates. It also makes it easier for the U.S. Embassy or consulate to contact you in an emergency. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Ambassador Carmen Moreno Toscano, a pioneering Mexican diplomat and a steadfast advocate for human rights and the advancement of women. Ambassador Moreno made an enduring contribution to the Organization of American States, first representing Mexico before the Organization and later serving for a decade as Executive Secretary of the Inter-American Commission of Women @CIMOEA. I had the pleasure and honor of working alongside her during some of those years. Through her leadership, she helped strengthen the inter-American agenda for women’s rights, political participation, equality, and the prevention and eradication of violence against women, including through the implementation of the Convention of Belém do Pará. Her wisdom, diplomatic skill, and lifelong commitment to public service earned her the respect and admiration of colleagues throughout the Americas. Her legacy will continue to inspire those working to build a more equal, just, and peaceful hemisphere. I extend my heartfelt condolences to her family, friends, former colleagues, and to the Government and people of #Mexico. When it comes to protecting the lives and livelihoods of our people, there is no Government or Opposition only Sri Lanka. Today, at the National Council for Disaster Management chaired by H.E the President, I shared a strategic science-backed proposal to help Sri Lanka prepare for the anticipated climate risks of 2026–27. My message was simple; we cannot afford to wait for disaster to strike we must act. By strengthening early warning systems, safeguarding our food and water security, and planning together as a nation, we can create greater resilience against climate change. NewsWire 🇱🇰 (@NewsWireLK) Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa has proposed a series of measures to strengthen Sri Lanka’s climate resilience and disaster preparedness, warning that the country should act now to prepare for the anticipated impacts of the 2026-2027 El Niño cycle. Speaking at the National Council for Disaster Management, chaired by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, Premadasa said climate security has become a national priority that requires a united, science-based response beyond political differences. Citing global scientific assessments, Premadasa warned that the developing El Niño could be among the strongest in recent decades, bringing prolonged droughts followed by severe flooding. He said Sri Lanka should move away from responding to disasters after they occur and instead adopt an anticipatory governance model based on scientific forecasting, risk assessments and early preparedness. Among his key proposals was making climate resilience a whole-of-government responsibility involving institutions responsible for agriculture, water resources, energy, health, finance, defence, provincial administration and local government. Premadasa also called for integrated reservoir management to improve water security, expansion of climate-smart agriculture to strengthen food security, and the modernisation of early warning systems through impact-based forecasting that provides communities with more actionable information before disasters strike. He further proposed strengthening disaster risk financing, improving preparedness for heatwaves and public health emergencies, enhancing the resilience of critical infrastructure, and establishing a National Climate Risk and Disaster Intelligence Centre to support evidence-based decision-making across Government. Premadasa said Sri Lanka should also draw lessons from countries such as India and Australia, which have strengthened climate forecasting, agricultural contingency planning and broader resilience initiatives in response to growing climate risks. Looking beyond the immediate El Niño threat, he proposed the preparation of a Presidential White Paper on National Climate Resilience and Disaster Preparedness to establish a long-term policy framework that would guide future governments. He stressed that climate resilience cannot be achieved by the Government alone and requires the participation of Parliament, provincial and local authorities, the scientific community, universities, the private sector, civil society, international development partners and local communities. Premadasa added that protecting the lives and livelihoods of Sri Lankans must remain a shared national responsibility. رسانه‌های پاکستانی گزارش داده‌اند که تجارت ترانزیت افغانستان و پاکستان در سال مالی ۲۰۲۶ پاکستان، به پایین‌ترین سطح خود رسیده و ارزش آن تنها ۳۶۷میلیون دالر بوده است. بر بنیاد این گزارش، ارزش تجارت ترانزیت میان دو کشور پیش از سال ۲۰۲۱ به حدود پنج میلیارد دالر می‌رسید و سالانه نزدیک به ۸۹هزار کانتینر میان دو کشور جابه‌جا می‌شد؛ اما این رقم در سال جاری به حدود ۱۱ هزار و ۶۰۰ کانتینر کاهش یافته است. بر پایه گزارش، تجارت ترانزیت میان افغانستان و پاکستان در سال ۲۰۲۳ از وضعیت مطلوبی برخوردار بود؛ به‌گونه‌ای که شمار کانتینرها از ۱۰۲ هزار فراتر رفت و ارزش آن ۶.۷ میلیارد دالر گزارش شد. در این گزارش آمده است که روی‌آوردن افغانستان به ایران به‌عنوان مسیر بدیل و نیز مسدود ماندن گذرگاه‌ها میان کابل و اسلام‌آباد، از عوامل اصلی این کاهش به شمار می‌روند. این گزارش همچنین می‌افزاید که افغانستان حتی پیش از بسته‌شدن گذرگاه‌ها نیز تجارت ترانزیت خود با پاکستان را کاهش داده و در پی گسترش همکاری‌های ترانزیتی و تجاری با ایران و کشورهای آسیای مرکزی بوده است. #طلوع‌نیوز

Efekt? Zniszczona infrastruktura odbudowana z plusem - w lepszej jakości bądź z nowymi funkcjonalnościami. Podsumowanie realnego wsparcia: 💸 ⁠Ponad 1 mld zł trafił bezpośrednio do 62 tys. rodzin - zasiłki z rezerwy MSWiA pozwoliły ludziom skutecznie odbudować domy i pomieszczenia gospodarcze. 💸 Samorządy sprawnie zamknęły bądź jeszcze realizują inwestycje – od dokumentacji, przez przetargi, aż po odbiór infrastruktury. Drogi, mosty i budynki użyteczności publicznej znów służą mieszkańcom. 💸 Fundusze unijne zostały w 100 proc. wykorzystane tam, gdzie były najbardziej potrzebne. Rządowa pomoc zadziałała szybko i skutecznie. Odbudowa po powodzi 2024 staje się faktem.

These assumptions matter because Iran is often viewed through the same flawed lens.
